chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام was asked about a man who became forgetful and did not know whether he had performed one sajdah or two. He said: He should perform one more sajdah, and after the completion of the salat, the two sajdahs of forgetfulness are not required upon him.

key_terms.أُخْرَى: one additional sajdah to complete what is uncertain
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat in which the doubt occurred
key_terms.سَجْدَةً: a single sajdah within the prayer
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed for forgetfulness
key_terms.سَهَا: became forgetful or inattentive during salat

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in salat if he doubts whether he performed one sajdah or two?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about doubt in the number of sajdahs during salat. If a person is unsure whether he performed one sajdah or two, he should perform one additional sajdah, and no sajdatā al-sahw are required after the prayer.
